title: Error Radar: Aggregated Anomaly Heatmap and Payload Dock
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design an integrated Console surface — the 'Error Radar' — that helps engineers find anomalous request patterns across routes and time, and a detachable 'Payload Dock' that surfaces compact request/response snapshots and diffs for rapid root-cause triage. This is targeted at the Console's main diagnostics page and the per-route timeline view.

Problem: Current error debugging flows require multiple clicks to fetch payloads, limited temporal context for retries, and no compact diff view for correlated failures. SREs and product engineers waste time reconstructing sequences or opening heavy payload panels, increasing MTTR.

Goals: Provide a single-glance heatmap for anomaly clusters, quick toggles to filter by severity taxonomy (client/server/resource/timeouts), and an inline, low-latency Payload Dock that pins request snapshots and shows a compact side-by-side diff with token/keys-level highlights. Support deep-linking and sharing snapshots for runbooks.

Key concepts: 1) Adaptive Anomaly Heatmap: aggregated errors by route x time using adaptive binning so small spikes remain visible without overwhelming noise. 2) Retry Swimlane: visualizes retry chains collapsed by default with expand-to-trace to show each attempt and backoff intervals. 3) Payload Dock: slide-over pane that docks to the right and can be detached into a floating snapshot; contains a compact diff view (JSON key-level changes, trimmed context), redacted sensitive fields, and a 'Pin for Compare' feature to compare two snapshots side-by-side. 4) Severity Taxonomy Filter: lightweight pill controls (client_error, transient, model_mismatch, infra) with count badges and the ability to fold low-severity noise.

Design constraints and non‑goals: Must render smoothly for up to 10k events in a query, rely on server-side aggregation for heavy queries (eng dependency ENG-4829). Payload Dock must not fetch full request bodies by default — show trimmed snapshot with a one-click reveal after RBAC check (ENG-4980 provides auth gating). Not a full replay system; we will not execute or re-run payloads from the UI in this iteration.

Accessibility & UX notes: Ensure keyboard focus for heatmap bins; color palette uses colorblind-safe ramp and also encodes severity with iconography to avoid color-only cues. Provide concise alt text for exported snapshots.

Deliverables: Annotated Figma prototype (desktop + condensed mobile), interaction spec for heatmap hover/zoom, acceptance criteria checklist, and an implementation handoff packet for Eng containing APIs required and recommended aggregation shapes.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Asha Patel (Design): Initial concept walkthrough with PM and Eng. Feedback: reduce default payload verbosity, add 'Pin for Compare' affordance, and include taxonomy presets for common customers.
2026-03-03 — Natasha Romero (PM): Prioritize client-visible error categories first. Suggested adding count-badges and quick-snooze for noisy routes.

2026-03-04 — Ben Chu (Eng): Reviewed prototype. Feasibility notes: server needs an aggregated bucket API and a lightweight snapshot endpoint behind RBAC. Will prototype an aggregated heatmap query to validate performance (ENG-4829).

2026-03-05 — Design Critique: Focused on micro-interactions: hover delay for heatmap, animation when expanding retry swimlane, and how pinned snapshots persist across sessions. Agreed next step: test with sample incident dataset and adjust adaptive bin sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap shows error density by route & 5m bins with an option to zoom into 1m bins; adaptive binning adjusts to avoid overplotting.
Clicking a heatmap cell opens a contextual list with retry swimlane collapsed by default and an option to expand to full attempt trace.
Payload Dock opens from any contextual list item; shows redacted snapshot, compact JSON diff, and a 'Pin for Compare' button.
Pinned snapshots can be compared side-by-side and shared via deep-link (URL) that encodes two snapshot IDs.
RBAC gating: full payload reveal requires an API token check; default view trims large bodies to 512 bytes (configurable).
Performance: heatmap renders 10k aggregated buckets on the client within 250ms on a mid-range laptop (progressive rendering allowed).
Accessibility: all interactive elements are keyboard-navigable and the heatmap has a textual summary for screen readers.
